description: The Eswatini Energy Regulatory Authority (ESERA) publishes a Fuel Station Supply and Demand Map to guide applications for fuel retail licences. It is an ArcGIS web experience backed by a public hosted feature service with five layers, read on 2026-09-29: 122 filling stations (name, company such as Engen, Galp, Puma, Total, Fuelex or Phakama Oil, number of pumps, town, coordinates, category, status, region and inkhundla code); 665 road links (road number, start and end kilometre, length, class, width, lanes, surface type and condition); 15 towns; 59 tinkhundla (constituency) polygons; and 2,326 supply and demand polygons scored on economic activity, traffic (AADT) density, fuel volume density, service ratio and distance to the nearest station, grouped into clusters and shown as over-supplied, balanced or under-supplied. The layers were last edited on 10 December 2025. Coverage: national, Eswatini. Format and access: web map and ArcGIS REST feature service (JSON, GeoJSON queries), free, no login. Licence: not stated; a disclaimer says the map is for information and decision support only. Caveats: updated as licences are issued, not on a fixed cycle; the demand scores are ESERA's model. Simulation uses: fuel supply resilience, emergency response routing and capacity planning of retail fuel networks. Related records: compare with Australia's national liquid fuel facilities (data-ga-national-liquid-fuel-facilities).
